fact: ITWeb Africa reports, on 2026-08-05 (no event date given, so the publication date), that consultations on Namibia's AI strategy framework have begun under NCRST leadership, per ICT Minister Emma Theofelus, with the strategy to precede AI legislation.

Tech Africa News reports that at a meeting on 3 August 2026 the ICT Minister said consultations on Namibia's Artificial Intelligence Strategy Framework had begun, led by the NCRST, and that a national AI strategy is prioritised before legislation.

NCRST's own authors state Namibia currently lacks a national AI strategy and is developing one through the NCRST AI Working Group and technical advisory committees; finalising it is a next step. Dated by publication, 2026-02-16.

NCRST officially commenced development of Namibia's first National AI Strategy and appointed Technical Advisory Committees, whose terms of reference were adopted at the inaugural meeting; dated by publication, 2025-09-08.
iAfrica says NCRST was assigned to lead development of Namibia's National AI Strategy, for which no date has been given; dated by publication, 2026-10-02.

The Namibian reports NCRST chief executive Anicia Peters saying the National AI Strategy, developed with 215 local experts and stakeholders and UNESCO, UNDP and KAS support, had reached synthesis and national validation, before the minister and then Cabinet.
CIPESA lists Namibia among countries still at different stages of developing their AI policies or strategies; no date of the stage is given, so the published date 2026-07-23 is used.
